User request: pasting two chunks out of the vendor msa. chunk A, page 4 section 3.2: 'either party may terminate for convenience upon ninety days written notice.' chunk B, page 11 section 7.1: 'termination for convenience does not relieve customer of fees accrued through the effective date.' if we walk away, what happens to the fees weve already run up, and show me where each piece of that sits so i can quote it in the memo

content.text:
Short answer
- If you (the Customer) “walk away” by giving a termination-for-convenience notice, you still owe the fees you have accrued up to the termination effective date. The notice right is in §3.2; the payment obligation is in §7.1.

Exact quotes and where to cite them in your memo
- §3.2 (p. 4): “either party may terminate for convenience upon ninety days written notice.” (MSA, p.4, §3.2)
- §7.1 (p. 11): “termination for convenience does not relieve customer of fees accrued through the effective date.” (MSA, p.11, §7.1)

How that operates (concise)
- Give written notice → termination becomes effective per the contract’s timing (the clause you quoted requires 90 days’ notice under §3.2) → you are responsible for all fees that have accrued through that effective date (per §7.1). In other words, you will owe charges for services/deliverables billed or incurred up to the termination effective date.

Short cautions / next checklist items to confirm before finalizing the memo
- Confirm whether the contract defines “effective date” or “accrued fees” elsewhere (definitions, billing, or payment sections)—that could affect the exact cutoff or what counts as “accrued.”
- Check for other related provisions (refunds for prepayments, minimum commitments, early-termination fees, return obligations, final invoicing timing) that could change the money owed.
- Review outstanding invoices and the vendor’s billing cycle to estimate the actual dollar amount owed through the effective date.

Suggested one-line citation for your memo
- “Per MSA, either party may terminate for convenience upon ninety days written notice (p.4, §3.2); termination for convenience ‘does not relieve customer of fees accrued through the effective date’ (p.11, §7.1).”

If you want, paste any related definition provisions (e.g., definition of “effective date” or “fees”) and I’ll confirm how they affect the amount due.
